data.long_meaning: A woman whose name signifies a burning desire, longing, or yearning. Derived from the verb 'raqqaqa' meaning to yearn or long. The name Ruqayqah carries the meaning “Intense, burning desire” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Ruqayqah usually hope their child will grow to embody intense, burning desire and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Ruqayqah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Intense, burning desire.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ruqayqah total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.
data.cultural_impact: In the Islamic context, Ruqayqah is mentioned in the Quran as the name of the wife of Prophet Hud (as). She was known for her patience and perseverance in the face of devastating drought and persistent infidelity from her husband and people. Prophet Hud (as) entreated his people to fear Allah and turn to Him for salvation, but they refused. Ruqayqah's unwavering belief and loyalty to her husband and faith inspired her people, but they would not listen. Eventually, Hud (as) and his family were sent to safety while the people of Ad were destroyed in a flood. As a result, the name Ruqayqah has lasted through the ages as a symbol of steadfastness and fortitude.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ruqayqah holds deep spiritual significance as it embodies the heartfelt yearning and longing for Allah. Ruqayqah's unwavering faith and commitment to her husband and Allah set an excellent example for Muslims to maintain unwavering faith and steadfastness through difficult trials. Furthermore, the name Ruqayqah represents the importance of continuing to seek Allah's forgiveness and guidance, even when facing hardships or difficulties. Just as Ruqayqah displayed immense patience and fortitude despite the challenging circumstances she faced, Muslims should strive to embody the name Ruqayqah by practicing patience and longing for Allah's siddiq (truth).
